newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX October power futures finish trade higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX October power futures finish trade higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mostly higher Wednesday on some shortcovering and generally stronger markets, industry sources said.
"The market is generally stronger, and combined with the October expiry that was enough to push it up," said one futures broker.
October California Oregon Border (COB) expired up 24 cents at $16.36 after trade in a range of $16.00-16.50, while November settled up 10 cents at $16.80 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Remaining COB deferreds closed up 10 cents.
October Palo Verde (PV) expired up 21 cents at $16.69 after trade in a range of $16.35-16.80, while November settled 25 cents higher at $15.55 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds ended between 15 and 25 cents higher.
NYMEX said an estimated 277 COB contracts and 214 PV contracts traded Thursday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
